design_doc.playbook/config-test-sync: When runtime config defaults change in shared_state.py, update corresponding test assertions: (1) max_active_directions (currently 10) → test_directions.py cap tests + test_invariants.py. (2) _max_review_iterations in review_pipeline.py (caps: small=10, ci_failure=8, medium=12, else=16) → test_pipeline_integration.py::test_review_fix_cap_* hardcoded iteration values must exceed cap to trigger.

Files: backend/app/time_utils.py, backend/app/compute.py, backend/app/github.py, backend/app/shared_state.py, backend/app/orchestrator.py. These tasks completed cleanly without review iterations despite this task type having prior failures in this project.
design_doc.playbook/review-type-safety: Review pattern from PR #1434 (3 iterations): type safety issues were repeatedly flagged. Examples: strVal(dirCtx.title as unknown) and strVal(dirCtx.priority as unknown) — since dirCtx is Record<string, unknown>, values are already typed as unknown. The 'as unknown' cast is redundant and can be dropped.. Applicable to: create tasks.
design_doc.playbook/review-test-coverage: Review pattern from PR #1434 (3 iterations): test coverage issues were repeatedly flagged. Examples: No backend test covers the new direction_context injection in the claim endpoint. test_agent.py has many /api/agent/claim tests but none sets up a direction with research_context and verifies direction_context appears in the response for create/fix/refactor tasks (and is absent for review tasks).; N. Applicable to: create tasks.
design_doc.playbook/research-direct-spawn: Research handler (research-plan.ts) directly spawns scope=small+risk=low implementation findings via /api/agent/spawn, marking them already_spawned:true in JSON output. Backend _handle_research_completion skips task creation for already_spawned findings but still counts them in research_history (tasks_created, finding_titles). Hash function is SHA-256(title+description)[:16] — same in Python and Node.js. Metadata types (direction_proposal/note/update, design_doc_observation, research) and non-small/non-low findings skip direct spawn and fall through to normal processing.
design_doc.playbook/admin-analytics-callers: compute_pipeline_health_summary (admin_analytics.py:270) imported by: routers/agent.py (deferred), test_pipeline_health.py, test_pipeline.py, test_agent.py. All use "from app.routers.admin_analytics import". _derive_completed_at is defined as inner function in BOTH compute_pipeline_health_summary (line 285) and get_digest (line 480) — consolidation opportunity.
design_doc.playbook/module-extraction-guide: When extracting functions/routes to new modules: (1) Create new router/module importing helpers from source. (2) Use AST-based scripts to find exact line ranges and remove by name. (3) Update main.py to include_router. (4) Grep ALL callers: test files, deferred imports inside function bodies, mocker.patch targets. Patch targets must match where symbol is DEFINED. (5) Check re-export blocks — some symbols are used by the exporting module itself. (6) After merge conflicts, verify resolution did not re-add extracted functions — FastAPI silently registers duplicates.
design_doc.playbook/react-hooks-v7-patterns: react-hooks v7 (eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.0.1) flags patterns v4 allowed: (1) setState(stateValue) inside useEffect — fix with useReducer or move to effects. (2) ref.current during render — move into effects. (3) Transitive tracking: useCallback that calls setState from useEffect triggers set-state-in-effect even after await. Use eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/set-state-in-effect for intentional async patterns — removing these disables causes build errors.
design_doc.playbook/project-field-ui-pattern: Adding a per-project JSONB field to the UI: add field in models.py + ProjectUpdate + GET serialization; add TypeScript types; expose setBuildConfig from useSettings; add updateBuildConfig+sync effect in useAppState; add projectOnly section to SettingsDropdown; wire through HeaderBar and App.
design_doc.playbook/task-ingestion-endpoints: 3 task ingestion endpoints: (1) /api/deploy at routers/projects.py:34 (user deploy), (2) /api/admin/tasks POST at admin.py:736 (admin manual create), (3) /api/agent/spawn at routers/agent.py:777 (agent-spawned subtasks). All store payloads as JSONB with per-type Pydantic validation (payload_schemas.py, 287 lines). Batch endpoints: /tasks/bulk-archive, /tasks/bulk-action.
design_doc.playbook/ws-ping-pong-close-codes: For WS ping/pong heartbeats: use ws.close(4001, 'Pong timeout') NOT 1000 when force-closing for reconnect — code 1000 is treated as intentional close and suppresses reconnect. Codes 4000-4999 are user-defined and safe to use from browser JS. Also initialize lastPongRef to 0 and compare lastPongRef.current < lastPingTime (not age check) to avoid false timeouts on connection open.
design_doc.playbook/acceptance-rate-data-flow: prs_rejected and avg_time_to_merge_hours are tracked per cycle in direction_outcomes.py (from ct.context.pr_rejected and vm_stopped_at-created_at delta). _compute_acceptance_rate in research_completion.py aggregates over history+history_aggregate, returns None for no-data. history_aggregate eviction now tracks total_prs_rejected. _direction_score tuple element added at position 4 (after merge_rate*momentum, before vision_rank). Strategic analysis and digest API both read these fields gracefully (null when absent).
design_doc.playbook/vm-cache-invalidation-gap: _ensure_vm_deleted (main.py) deletes the VM but does not immediately update the cached VM count. _get_actual_gcp_vm_count uses 120s cache TTL. This creates phantom slots where the system thinks more VMs are running than actually are. Structural gap persists — not a bug, but a design limitation that can cause brief over-provisioning.
design_doc.playbook/auto-remediation-task-type: Auto-remediation fix tasks for main-branch CI failures should use task type 'create' (not 'fix'), because 'fix' requires pr_number and branch of an existing PR. The create task spawns a new branch, applies fix, opens PR — then the standard review pipeline handles review/merge. Include context.auto_remediation=True to distinguish from regular create tasks.
design_doc.playbook/cost-window-filter-pattern: When computing per-window cost metrics in admin_analytics.py (e.g. for 24h dashboard cards), always apply 'and t.vm_stopped_at >= window_start' to filter expressions. The all_tasks query uses a 7-day extended lookback; omitting the window filter inflates headline numbers by up to 7x vs the label.
design_doc.playbook/pr-rejection-signal-fields: pr_rejected=True and pr_rejection_note (PR body, up to 500 chars) are set on task.context by the pull_request webhook handler when a PR is closed without merge. prs_rejected counter accumulates in direction_outcomes.py research_history entries (alongside prs_merged). history_aggregate also tracks total_prs_rejected for evicted cycles. _compute_merge_rate penalizes rejections at -0.5x weight vs merges (+1x). strategic_analysis.py and strategic_spawning.py expose operator_rejection_rate = rejected/(merged+rejected) only when total_rejected > 0.
design_doc.playbook/review-pipeline-test-mocks: When testing _spawn_pipeline_task directly: mock 'app.review_pipeline.broadcast_to_project' (module-level import) as AsyncMock. For stuck-cycle tests that trigger the notification path, also mock 'app.notification_dispatch.dispatch_external_notification' as AsyncMock to avoid ensure_future scheduling a failing coroutine.
design_doc.playbook/failure-class-not-persisted: failure_class is computed on-read by classify_failure() (failure_classification.py:21-124) every time. Never stored on Task model or in task.context. Two parallel classifiers exist: classify_failure (comprehensive, in failure_classification.py) and _classify_stuck_failure (admin_settings.py:66, lightweight subset that delegates to classify_failure, returns None for CODE_ERROR). CatchUpPanel is the canonical UI pattern for failure_class badges (color-coded: CODE_ERROR=red, RATE_LIMIT/EXTERNAL_API=amber).
design_doc.playbook/fastapi-409-response-format: FastAPI HTTPExceptions are caught by a custom handler (main.py @app.exception_handler(HTTPException) at line 1077) that wraps the response as {error: {code: status_code, message: detail}} — NOT the default FastAPI {detail: message} format. Tests asserting error detail must use resp.json()[error][message], not resp.json()[detail]. This handler applies to ALL HTTP status codes. Inline 409 responses also exist at lines 1635 and 1644 as direct JSONResponse returns.
design_doc.playbook/frontend-ceiling-no-ratchet: test_invariants.py FRONTEND_SIZE_LIMITS and MODULE_SIZE_LIMITS comments explicitly say 'do NOT ratchet down the limit after every cleanup — these limits should stay stable.' These are loose upper bounds for catching runaway growth, not tight ceilings. Existing multipliers: frontend ~2-4x actual size, backend ~1.5-2.5x.
design_doc.playbook/orchestrator-filter-pattern: New dispatch filters go in orchestrator_filters.py following the async function pattern (eligible_ids, candidate_tasks, active_tasks, session, broadcast_fn) -> list[uuid.UUID]. orchestrator_filters.py does NOT import runtime_config — it receives all config through function parameters. Register in orchestrator.py and call between Step 2.6 and slot-cap.
design_doc.playbook/task-type-hints-buildconfig: getTaskTypeHints(buildConfig) in prompt.ts replaces TASK_TYPE_HINTS static map for dynamic hint generation. Falls back to static TASK_TYPE_HINTS when buildConfig.directories is empty. specialized.ts no longer imports TASK_TYPE_HINTS (removed — unused); uses getTaskTypeHints instead. Mocks in standard.test.ts and specialized.test.ts need both TASK_TYPE_HINTS:{} and getTaskTypeHints:vi.fn().mockReturnValue({}) entries.
design_doc.playbook/check-run-webhook-branch-data: GitHub check_run webhook payload includes check_suite.head_branch (the branch name) and check_suite.pull_requests (empty array for non-PR commits). Handler at routers/github.py:441 extracts head_branch via (check_run.get(check_suite) or {}).get(head_branch) and uses it for auto-remediation on protected branches.
design_doc.playbook/webhook-url-masking-non-admin: GET /api/admin/settings returns notification_config to all auth'd users (get_current_user). Webhook URLs (Slack/PagerDuty/Discord) embed auth tokens, so mask webhook_url for non-admin callers: return empty string + webhook_url_configured:bool flag. Pattern: _build_notification_config_response(config, is_admin=current_user.get('role')=='admin') in admin_settings.py. Admin callers get full URL.
design_doc.playbook/conversion-rate-metric-pattern: conversion_rate = prs_merged / tasks_created (per research_history entry) computed in direction_outcomes.py after prs_merged update. Digest API sums tasks_created from research_history window entries (not from task DB count). compute_pipeline_health_summary returns pipeline_conversion_rate (pipeline aggregate) + per-direction conversion_rate in direction_stats. Agent aggregateDirectionStats uses history.slice(-3) for 'last N cycles' label. _safe_ts_in_window helper added to compute_pipeline_health_summary for timestamp comparisons.
design_doc.playbook/requeue-classify-before-cancel: In _requeue_parent_task, always capture failure_class = classify_failure(child) AND original_status_message = child.latest_status_message BEFORE setting child.status = CANCELLED and overwriting latest_status_message. Both are used for retry guidance injection — reading after cancellation sees the overwritten values.
design_doc.playbook/deferred-import-admin-from-main: Import symbols from other app modules inside function bodies (not at module level) to avoid circular dependencies between router modules. main.py itself uses top-level imports, but router modules still use deferred imports for cross-module references. _SEED_ENTRIES pattern in routers/admin_notifications.py (line 50) is an example of module-level data that other modules should NOT import at top level. Note: orchestrator_filters.py does NOT use deferred imports — it has no runtime_config dependency.
design_doc.playbook/task-lifecycle-head-sha-unbound: head_sha in task_lifecycle.py is pre-initialized to empty string at line ~765 before the APPROVE try block. The conditional reassignment (from pr_data and for review cycle) are within try blocks. Original UnboundLocalError risk mitigated by pre-initialization. Pattern still requires care if restructuring the APPROVE flow.
design_doc.playbook/vitest-setupWorkspace-signature: When setupWorkspace signature changes (new optional params added), update standard.test.ts assertions — they use toHaveBeenCalledWith with exact arg count. Each handler's branchPrefix test has a separate assertion; replace_all won't catch all if surrounding context differs.
design_doc.playbook/classify-stuck-failure-canonica: _classify_stuck_failure in admin_settings.py now delegates to classify_failure() from failure_classification.py, returning None for CODE_ERROR (since stuck tasks haven't failed yet). When updating tests, use canonical classifier's exact keyword strings — e.g. 'vm failed to start' not 'vm failed', '503 service unavailable' not '503 unavailable'.
design_doc.playbook/orchestrator-filter-mock-patter: When testing filter functions in orchestrator_filters.py, use patch.dict(app.shared_state.runtime_config, {...}) NOT patch(app.orchestrator_filters.runtime_config, ...). Note: orchestrator_filters.py itself does NOT import runtime_config — it receives configuration through function parameters. The deferred import pattern applies to other modules like orchestrator.py and routers/directions.py.
design_doc.playbook/rollup-retry-re-enters-full-flo: Rollup retry (rollup_management.py) does NOT retry inline — leaves parent EVALUATING and lets orchestrator CI monitoring loop re-enter _check_and_trigger_rollup on next cycle, including staging branch validation. Exception handler includes invalidate_github_token_cache() for auth failures.
design_doc.playbook/session-commit-exclusion-patter: When a function queries the DB for in-flight objects that were just modified in-memory before the query (pre-commit), exclude the current object via 'Task.id != task.id' and add its contribution manually after the loop. This is robust regardless of autoflush settings and avoids one-task-late alerts.
design_doc.playbook/vitest-mock-runProjectLintCheck: review-fix.ts imports runProjectLintChecks from ../index.js (used at line 514 for fix handler). When mocking ../index.js in agent handler tests, include runProjectLintChecks in the mock. Note: no review-fix.test.ts currently exists — this guidance applies if one is created or if other test files mock ../index.js comprehensively.
design_doc.playbook/webhook-dispatch-fire-and-forge: Use asyncio.ensure_future(dispatch_external_notification(...)) at call sites — not await — so webhook HTTP calls never block the main request path. dispatch_external_notification itself never raises. _last_dispatch_time is module-level dict in notification_dispatch.py keyed by event_type for per-event throttling.
design_doc.playbook/agent-status-flag-modified-impo: agent_status.py does NOT import flag_modified by default (it's in agent.py). When modifying design_doc in agent_status.py, add 'from sqlalchemy.orm.attributes import flag_modified' to the imports.
design_doc.playbook/payload-schema-per-type-field-m: 17 task types exist (create, refactor, review, fix, plan, research, strategic_review, design_doc_update, security_audit, qa, deps, docs, smoketest, migrate, debug, perf, investigate). Handler registry in agent/src/handlers/index.ts:14-32. Required fields per type: create/refactor/plan/migrate need prompt; review needs pr_number+branch; fix needs pr_number+branch+prompt. Research/strategic_review/design_doc_update have no required fields because backend populates them. All types share optional: base_branch, model, effort, prompt_suffix.
design_doc.playbook/strategic-prompt-message-handli: Strategic agent (research-plan.ts) has two passes. Thinker (Pass 1, line 728): builds context with open messages as ## Open Messages with resolve instructions. Executor (Pass 2, line 780): focused only on running ./strategic and ./design-doc commands. Modify BOTH passes when adding message-driven behavior.
design_doc.playbook/task-payloads-plural-not-singul: The claim endpoint returns task.payloads (plural array), not task.payload (singular). In agent TypeScript code, always access the first payload as: const payloads = Array.isArray(task.payloads) ? task.payloads as Record<string, unknown>[] : []; const payload = payloads[0]. The index.ts handler already does this correctly; buildContextPrefix in prompt.ts had this bug where it used task.payload directly.
design_doc.playbook/installation-webhook-inner-patt: Background handlers that open their own AsyncSessionLocal should split into an outer function (opens session) and an _inner function (takes session). Tests call _inner directly with db_session. Follow auto_remediation.py pattern. Mocks: patch 'app.github.get_repo_installation_token' and 'app.routers.admin_onboard._detect_build_config' (deferred imports — patch where defined, not where called).
design_doc.playbook/verify-agent-token-terminal-exe: verify_agent_token in routers/agent.py (line 99) rejects tokens for terminal tasks by default. The /api/agent/status endpoint is exempt via path check at lines 117 and 136. Uses _terminated_task_ids cache (O(1) fast path) + TTL cache for recently verified active tasks + DB fallback.
design_doc.playbook/vitest-react-hook-interval-leak: When testing hooks with setInterval: call cleanup() in BOTH beforeEach and afterEach. Without it, intervals leak across tests causing act() hangs. For fake timers, use vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setInterval','clearInterval'] }) — do NOT fake setImmediate (React scheduler uses it).
design_doc.playbook/direction-summary-injection-pat: When research_completion.py spawns implementation tasks, it injects direction_summary into task.context: {id, title, priority, failed_approaches[], recent_outcomes[]}. Built by _build_direction_summary() which parses direction.research_context via _parse_research_context(). standard.ts reads task.context.direction_summary and renders a '## Direction Context' section appended to contextPrefix before parentCtx.
design_doc.playbook/filter-test-session-refresh-pat: When testing orchestrator_filters.py: the filter updates task.latest_status_message in-memory + calls session.add(task) but does NOT commit. In tests with autoflush=False, calling await session.refresh(task) after the filter re-reads from DB (overwriting in-memory changes). Assert on the in-memory attribute directly instead of refreshing, OR call await session.flush() before refresh.
design_doc.playbook/rollup-review-iteration-cap-sha: Rollup reviews share per-PR iteration counting with regular review-fix cycles (review_pipeline.py:96-114). When a rollup PR accumulates iterations across retry attempts (same PR number reused), the cap permanently blocks future review spawns. rollup_management.py:627-628 then fails the parent as CODE_ERROR. 5 failures in 48h traced to PR #872. Fix: detect rollup source tasks and use MAX_REVIEW_FIX_ITERATIONS (16) instead of scope-based cap.
design_doc.playbook/settings-section-extraction-pat: When adding a new settings tab to SettingsDropdown.tsx: (1) Create a standalone section component in its own file following SettingsAdvancedSection.tsx/SettingsDeploySection.tsx pattern, (2) Export a named type for its config shape, (3) Add 'notifications' to SectionId union, add entry to SECTIONS array, add case in renderActiveSection(), (4) Add state to useSettings.ts + fetchSettings loader + PATCH handler, (5) Wire through HeaderBar.tsx props interface, HeaderBar SettingsDropdown call, useAppState.ts destructuring and return, and App.tsx HeaderBar call.
design_doc.playbook/strategic-spawning-type-conditi: force_strategic in autonomous_research.py (not strategic_spawning.py) spawns either design_doc_update (architecture cycles: strategic_cycle_count % arch_frequency == 0) or strategic_review (strategy-only cycles). Tests asserting only design_doc_update type should accept either. Default arch_frequency=3, so cycle 1 spawns strategic_review, cycle 3 spawns design_doc_update. The force_strategic flag triggers when: no vision purpose, no active directions, or all directions saturated (unless strategic_failures >= 3).
design_doc.playbook/provision-failure-escalation-pa: PROVISION_FAILURE surge pattern caused by compounding factors: (1) zone cooldown exponential backoff (compute.py) caps at 30min (1800s) — after 3 consecutive zone failures, cooldown reaches ~24min; (2) VM cache invalidation gap — _ensure_vm_deleted deletes VM but cached count may lag 120s, creating phantom slots; (3) all-zones-cooled-down path waits up to 5min (ZONE_RECOVERY_WAIT_CAP_SECONDS=300) for soonest recovery then permanent failure. provision_zone only saved on heartbeat (orchestrator.py), not at provision time.
design_doc.playbook/admin-analytics-approval-tasks-: In get_digest (admin_analytics.py), approval_tasks is independently derived from the all_tasks extended lookback query (lines 501-506), filtering on requires_approval=True, status not in (COMPLETED, FAILED), and created_at >= window_start. It is NOT derived from active_tasks_all (the QUEUED/PROVISIONING/IN_PROGRESS/EVALUATING query). These are two distinct queries with different filtering logic.
design_doc.playbook/settings-new-section-addtoast-p: When adding a new section to SettingsDropdown, it needs an addToast prop for user feedback. addToast is returned from useAppState (via useToasts inside it) and must be: (1) added to SettingsDropdown props, (2) added to HeaderBar props, (3) passed from App.tsx as s.addToast. Also, fetchProjects must be explicitly added to the useAppState return object before it can be passed as onProjectUpdated.
design_doc.playbook/vm-stopped-at-only-on-agent-com: vm_stopped_at is set in routers/agent_status.py:733 when the agent reports terminal status. This is the single assignment point — reaper.py, services.py, and orchestrator.py do NOT set vm_stopped_at directly. Guard: if task.vm_provisioned_at and not task.vm_stopped_at prevents double-write.
design_doc.playbook/research-completion-project-loa: When injecting project/direction data into child tasks in _handle_research_completion (research_completion.py), load the project with 'await session.get(Project, task.project_id)' BEFORE the child task creation loop. SQLAlchemy identity map means subsequent 'session.get' calls for the same project in the same session return the cached object — no performance concern. Build a _directions_by_id dict from project.directions for O(1) lookups inside the loop.
design_doc.playbook/strategic-api-skipped-response-: Skipped direction responses now return HTTP 409 with body containing status:skipped and reason field but NO op field. Agent helper handles 409 specially - prints CONSTRAINT marker to stderr. Post-check detects via CONSTRAINT regex or status:skipped regex. Both detection paths properly prevent retries.

directions.text: First-attempt code quality is the throughput engine. Inject direction context, scope constraints, and review pattern guidance into create/fix/refactor agents. Track first-attempt APPROVE rate as the primary metric. Every percentage point improvement eliminates a full review-fix-review cycle (15-30 min compute per task). Target: first-attempt APPROVE rate from ~30% to 50%+.

directions.text: Research-to-merge pipeline efficiency. CRITICAL DEADLOCK: the dedup false-positive bug (9-stopword / 3-shared-word threshold) may be blocking its own fix — 0 merges this window despite 7 proposed findings. If autonomous pipeline cannot break through within 1 cycle, escalate for manual intervention. Immediate goal: land the dedup fix. Then: auto-spawn create tasks for known-bug-known-fix patterns, fix finding-to-task scoping, surface finding-to-merge conversion rate.

directions.text: Self-test coverage on frequently-modified modules prevents regressions that cost full debug-fix-review cycles. Only 13 of 52 backend modules have direct test files. Focus coverage on the modules the system modifies most: autonomous loop, research completion, review pipeline, task lifecycle. Every regression prevented is a cycle saved. Measure: test coverage percentage on the 10 most-frequently-modified modules.
